grammar_rules.summary: The feminine form of an adjective is often created by adding -e to the masculine form.
grammar_rules.explanation: To form the feminine of many adjectives, add -e to the masculine form. The final consonant of the masculine form is silent, while the final consonant of the feminine form is pronounced.
usage: To form feminine adjectives from masculine adjectives.
exceptions: Adjectives ending in -e in masculine remain unchanged in feminine.
agreement_rules: Feminine adjectives agree with feminine nouns.
common_traps: Do not pronounce the final consonant of the masculine form, but do pronounce it in the feminine form.

attestations.source_text: The feminine form of an adjective is very often created by adding an -e to the masculine form.

grammar_rules.summary: Adjectives ending in -e in the masculine form remain unchanged in the feminine form.
grammar_rules.explanation: If an adjective ends with an -e in the masculine form, the feminine form is identical.

attestations.source_text: If an adjective ends with an -e in the masculine form, the feminine form remains the same.

grammar_rules.summary: Some adjectives have irregular feminine forms, often involving consonant changes or doubling.
grammar_rules.explanation: Certain adjectives have irregular feminine forms: vietnamien -> vietnamienne, italien -> italienne, généreux -> généreuse, dangereux -> dangereuse, interactif -> interactive, passif -> passive, faux -> fausse.
usage: To form feminine of irregular adjectives.
agreement_rules: Feminine forms agree with feminine nouns.
common_traps: Do not assume all adjectives add -e.

grammar_rules.summary: Certain adjectives have a special masculine singular form before a noun starting with a vowel.
grammar_rules.explanation: Adjectives fou, vieux, nouveau, beau have special forms fol, vieil, nouvel, bel when preceding a masculine singular noun beginning with a vowel sound.
grammar_rules.formation: fou -> fol, vieux -> vieil, nouveau -> nouvel, beau -> bel
usage: Before masculine singular nouns starting with a vowel.
restrictions: Only before masculine singular nouns starting with a vowel sound.
common_traps: Use special forms only before masculine singular nouns starting with a vowel.

grammar_rules.summary: In French, most qualificative adjectives follow the noun they modify.
grammar_rules.explanation: The default position for French adjectives is after the noun.
exceptions: Some short, common adjectives precede the noun.
common_traps: Do not place all adjectives before the noun.

attestations.source_text: In French, most qualificative adjectives follow the noun.

grammar_rules.summary: Certain short, common adjectives precede the noun; these must be memorized.
grammar_rules.explanation: Adjectives such as long, beau, nouveau, bon, mauvais, vieux, jeune precede the noun.
usage: For a limited set of common adjectives.
restrictions: Specific adjectives: long, beau, nouveau, bon, mauvais, vieux, jeune.
conditions: Adjective is one of the listed ones.
signal_words: long, beau, nouveau, bon, mauvais, vieux, jeune
common_traps: Do not place other adjectives before the noun.

attestations.source_text: Some adjectives precede the noun. You just need to memorize them.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Adjectives change meaning based on position
grammar_rules.summary: Some adjectives have different meanings depending on whether they precede or follow the noun.
grammar_rules.explanation: Adjectives like ancien, cher, pauvre, propre, sale, grand, dernier have distinct meanings when placed before or after the noun.
restrictions: Only certain adjectives have this property.
conditions: Adjective is one of: ancien, cher, pauvre, propre, sale, grand, dernier.
signal_words: ancien, cher, pauvre, propre, sale, grand, dernier
common_traps: Misinterpreting the adjective's meaning based on position.

attestations.source_text: Beware: Some adjectives have different meanings, depending on whether they precede or follow the noun.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Color adjectives agree in gender and number
grammar_rules.summary: Adjectives describing colors usually agree in gender and number with the noun they modify.
grammar_rules.explanation: Color adjectives follow normal agreement rules.
conditions: Adjective is a simple color adjective.
exceptions: Color adjectives derived from nouns (orange, marron, safran) and compound color adjectives are invariable.
agreement_rules: Agree in gender and number with noun.

attestations.source_text: Adjectives describing colors usually agree in gender and number with the noun they modify.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Color adjectives from nouns are invariable
grammar_rules.summary: Adjectives of color that are also nouns of fruit or plants remain in the masculine singular form.
grammar_rules.explanation: Orange, marron, safran are invariable because they originate as nouns.
usage: For color adjectives derived from fruit/plant nouns.
restrictions: Only for specific color adjectives: orange, marron, safran.
conditions: Adjective is one of orange, marron, safran.
common_traps: Do not make these adjectives agree.

attestations.source_text: Adjectives of color that are also nouns of fruit or plants generally remain in the masculine singular form.

grammar_rules.summary: When two adjectives are combined to provide more specificity, both adjectives generally remain in the masculine singular form.
grammar_rules.explanation: Compound color adjectives like vert clair, gris foncé, rose bonbon, bleu azur, châtain clair do not agree.
common_traps: Do not make compound color adjectives agree.

attestations.source_text: When two adjectives are combined to provide more specificity, both adjectives generally remain in the masculine singular form.

grammar_rules.explanation: To compare, use plus (more), moins (less), aussi (as) followed by que.
grammar_rules.formation: plus + adjective/adverb + que / moins + adjective/adverb + que / aussi + adjective/adverb + que
common_traps: Do not use 'que' after plus/moins/aussi when followed by de with nouns.

attestations.source_text: In French, comparisons of adjectives and adverbs can take three forms, plus... que (more . . . than), moins... que (less . . . than), aussi... que (as . . . as).

grammar_rules.summary: To compare quantities, use plus de, moins de, autant de.
grammar_rules.explanation: For nouns, use plus de (more), moins de (less), autant de (as much/many) with de.
grammar_rules.formation: plus de + noun / moins de + noun / autant de + noun
common_traps: Use de, not que, directly after plus/moins/autant when comparing nouns.

attestations.source_text: To compare quantities, use the following expressions. Note the use of de (d’) with expressions of quantity:

grammar_rules.summary: Some comparatives have irregular forms: bon -> meilleur, bien -> mieux, mauvais -> pire, petit -> moindre (implied).
grammar_rules.explanation: Bon becomes meilleur (better), bien becomes mieux (better), mauvais becomes pire (worse).
grammar_rules.formation: bon -> meilleur, bien -> mieux, mauvais -> pire
agreement_rules: Meilleur and pire agree as adjectives; mieux is adverb.
common_traps: Do not say 'plus bon' or 'plus bien'.

grammar_rules.summary: Superlative is formed by preceding the comparative with the definite article; before a group, use de + definite article.
grammar_rules.explanation: To form the superlative, use le/la/les + plus/moins + adjective. When specifying the group, add de + definite article.
usage: To express the most, least, best, worst.
agreement_rules: Article and adjective agree with noun.
grammar_rules.word_order: definite article + plus/moins + adjective + (de + definite article + group)
common_traps: Remember to add de + definite article after superlative when mentioning the group.

attestations.source_text: To form the superlative in French, simply precede the comparative form by the definite article. Note that before naming a group or entity, the superlative is followed by de  the definite article.

grammar_rules.summary: Irregular adjectives use their irregular comparative forms in the superlative: bon -> le meilleur, mauvais -> le pire.
grammar_rules.explanation: Bon becomes le meilleur, mauvais becomes le pire.
usage: For superlative of bon and mauvais.
agreement_rules: Meilleur and pire agree with noun.

attestations.source_text: The irregular adjectives you learned with the comparatives are also used in the superlative.
